T: First class dinner. Third class party.
D: A poor artist and an upper-class woman fall in love aboard the doomed ocean liner.
P: Serve the mains when Jack joins Rose's family for dinner in first class.
S: Fresh shucked oysters on ice with lemon and shallot mignonette
Freshly shucked oysters on crushed ice with a shallot and red wine vinegar mignonette and lemon.
King of the world ham sandwiches
Crusty ham and English mustard sandwiches with buttered small potatoes

Thick slices of leg ham with hot English mustard on buttered crusty bread, with small potatoes boiled in their skins and tossed in butter and salt. Butter thick slices of a crusty loaf and fill with 300g ham and hot English mustard. Boil 600g small potatoes in their skins and toss with butter and salt. Serve together below deck.
a dish from the real first class menu that night

Salmon gently poached in a lemon and herb court bouillon, chilled and flaked onto toasts with a light mousseline of hollandaise folded with whipped cream. Simmer 1L water with a sliced lemon, a bay leaf, peppercorns, dill stalks and a splash of vinegar for 10 minutes. Add a 400g salmon fillet, turn off the heat and leave 12 minutes, then chill and flake. Whisk 2 yolks with 1 tbsp lemon juice over simmering water until thick, then drizzle in 100g warm melted butter. Fold in 80ml softly whipped cream. Toast 16 baguette slices and top with salmon, mousseline and dill.
M: Molly Brown's first class filet mignon
Seared tied eye fillet with pommes Anna, the layered potato cake

Eye fillet steaks tied, seared hard in butter, roasted at 200C to 54C and rested, with a red wine and shallot sauce reduced with stock, pommes Anna and buttered green beans. Layer 800g thinly sliced potatoes with 60g melted butter in a pan and bake at 200C for 50 minutes for pommes Anna. Tie 4 eye fillet steaks, sear in butter and roast to 54C. Reduce 2 shallots, 200ml red wine and 250ml stock for sauce. Serve with 300g green beans.
First class lamb rack with mint sauce
a dish straight off the real first class menu that night

Lamb racks seared and roasted pink, carved into cutlets, with fresh sharp mint sauce, buttery minted peas and crisp roast potatoes. Parboil 1kg potatoes and roast in oil at 220C for 50 minutes. Season 2 lamb racks, sear fat side down, roast at 200C to 56C inside, about 15 minutes, and rest 10 minutes. Chop a bunch of mint with 2 tbsp sugar, 3 tbsp boiling water and 4 tbsp malt vinegar. Cook 400g peas with 30g butter and chopped mint. Carve the racks into cutlets.
W: Baked custard with apples and sultanas, nutmeg on top
Apples peeled, diced and cooked in butter with sultanas, spooned into a dish, covered in a vanilla custard of eggs, milk and sugar with nutmeg, baked in a water bath at 160C for 40 minutes.
K: Black velvet, stout and sparkling wine
Irish stout layered under chilled sparkling wine in tall flutes

Rich Irish stout poured half and half with cold sparkling wine in tall flutes, steerage on the bottom and first class on top. Chill a 750ml bottle of sparkling wine and four 440ml cans of Irish stout. Half fill four tall flutes or glasses with stout, poured slowly so it settles. Top each slowly with sparkling wine poured over the back of a spoon so it sits on top. Serve straight away.
